title: Lodge a cease to trade notification
summary: Lodging a cease to trade notification is required if you plan to temporarily stop trading for six weeks or longer.
intro:
If you want to temporarily cease trading for 6 weeks or longer, you need to lodge a cease to trade notification.

Even though you have temporarily ceased trading, you're still subject to the annual liquor licence fee.

When the licensed premises is ready to recommence trading, you will need to lodge a recommence trading application through the liquor licence manager.

If the licensed premises is ceasing to trade permanently, you'll need to complete the surrender liquor licence application.

For up-to-date liquor licence guidelines, resources and tools visit Liquor & Gaming NSW liquor licensing.

If you have questions or feedback about liquor licensing contact Liquor & Gaming NSW.
what_you_need: The liquor licence name and number
Personal details (if you are an individual)
ABN, ACN, and Y/Inc (if you are an organisation)
Personal details and residential and/or postal address for the contact person

how_to_steps.text: Select the ‘Go to Liquor Licence Manager’ button.
Log in, or create your MyServiceNSW Account.
Select 'View details' for the required licence.
Go to 'Cease to trade' and select 'Apply'.
Follow the prompts to submit your cease to trade application.

faqs.q: What do I do if I temporarily stop trading for 6 weeks or longer?
faqs.a: You need to lodge a cease to trade notification.

faqs.q: Do I still have to pay the annual liquor licence fee if I temporarily stop trading?
faqs.a: Yes, you are still subject to the annual liquor licence fee.

faqs.q: What happens when I want to start trading again?
faqs.a: When the licensed premises is ready to recommence trading, you must lodge a recommence trading application through the liquor licence manager.

faqs.q: What if I am permanently closing my business?
faqs.a: If the licensed premises is ceasing to trade permanently, you must complete the surrender liquor licence application.
